question: What did NASA's Europa Clipper spacecraft do during its Mars flyby in 2025, and when is it due to reach Jupiter?
text:
On **March 1, 2025**, NASA’s Europa Clipper flew about **550 miles (884 kilometers)** above Mars, using the planet’s gravity to bend its trajectory toward Jupiter. During the flyby, it took infrared images of Mars to calibrate its thermal camera and tested its ice-penetrating radar as a complete system for the first time. ([science.nasa.gov](https://science.nasa.gov/mission/europa-clipper/mission-timeline/?utm_source=openai))

Europa Clipper is scheduled to **enter orbit around Jupiter in April 2030**. ([science.nasa.gov](https://science.nasa.gov/mission/europa-clipper/mission-timeline/?utm_source=openai))
